query: We then measured the size of the axon-spine interface of SynEM detected synapses in the test set (Figure 7a,b). We find an average axon-spine interface size of 0.263 ± 0.206 µm2 (mean ± s.d.; range 0.033–1.189 µm2; n = 181), consistent with previous reports (de Vivo et al., 2017: (SW) 0.297 ± 0.297 µm2 (p=0.518, two-sample two-tailed t-test on the natural logarithm of the axon-spine interface size), (EW) 0.284 ± 0.275 µm2 (p=0.826, two-sample two-tailed t-test on the natural logarithm of the axon-spine interface size). This indicates that, first, synapse detection in our lower-resolution SBEM data (in-plane image resolution about 11 nm, section thickness about 26–30 nm) yields similar synapse size distributions as in the higher-resolution data in de Vivo et al. (2017) (in-plane image resolution 5.9 nm; section thickness about 50 nm) and secondly, that SynEM-based synapse detection has no obvious bias towards larger synapses.

query: We report SynEM, a toolset for automated synapse detection in EM-based connectomics. The particular achievement is that the synapse detection for densely mapped connectomes from the mammalian cerebral cortex is fully automated yielding below 3% residual error in the binary connectome.
matched_segment: We report SynEM, a toolset for automated synapse detection in EM-based connectomics. The particular achievement is that the synapse detection for densely mapped connectomes from the mammalian cerebral cortex is fully automated yielding below 3% residual error in the binary connectome.

query: Importantly, SynEM directly provides the location and size of synapses, the involved neurites and the synapse direction without human interaction.
matched_segment: Importantly, SynEM directly provides the location and size of synapses, the involved neurites and the synapse direction without human interaction.

query: With this, synapse detection is removed as a bottleneck in large-scale mammalian connectomics.
matched_segment: With this, synapse detection is removed as a bottleneck in large-scale mammalian connectomics.

query: Evidently, synapse detection is facilitated in high-resolution EM data, and becomes most feasible in FIB-SEM data at a resolution of about 4–8 nm isotropic (Kreshuk et al., 2011, Figure 3f).
matched_segment: Evidently, synapse detection is facilitated in high-resolution EM data, and becomes most feasible in FIB-SEM data at a resolution of about 4–8 nm isotropic (Kreshuk et al., 2011, Figure 3f).

query: Yet, only by compromising resolution for speed (and thus volume) of imaging, the mapping of large, potentially even whole-brain connectomes is becoming plausible (Figure 3f).
matched_segment: Yet, only by compromising resolution for speed (and thus volume) of imaging, the mapping of large, potentially even whole-brain connectomes is becoming plausible (Figure 3f).

query: The fact that SynEM also outperforms state-of-the-art methods on high-resolution anisotropic 3D EM data (Figure 3f, Roncal et al., 2015) indicates that our approach of segmentation-based interface classification has merits in a wider range of 3D EM data modalities.
matched_segment: The fact that SynEM also outperforms state-of-the-art methods on high-resolution anisotropic 3D EM data (Figure 3f, Roncal et al., 2015) indicates that our approach of segmentation-based interface classification has merits in a wider range of 3D EM data modalities.

query: In addition to high image resolution, recently proposed special fixation procedures that enhance the extracellular space in 3D EM data (Pallotto et al., 2015) are reported to simplify synapse detection for human annotators.
matched_segment: In addition to high image resolution, recently proposed special fixation procedures that enhance the extracellular space in 3D EM data (Pallotto et al., 2015) are reported to simplify synapse detection for human annotators.

query: In such data, direct touch between neurites has a very high predictive power for the existence of a (chemical or electrical) synapse, since otherwise neurite boundaries are separated by extracellular space.
matched_segment: In such data, direct touch between neurites has a very high predictive power for the existence of a (chemical or electrical) synapse, since otherwise neurite boundaries are separated by extracellular space.

query: Thus, it is expected that such data also substantially simplifies automated synapse detection.
matched_segment: Thus, it is expected that such data also substantially simplifies automated synapse detection.

query: The advantage of SynEM is that it achieves fully automated synapse detection in conventionally stained and fixated 3D EM data, in which neurite contact is most frequent at non-synaptic sites.
matched_segment: The advantage of SynEM is that it achieves fully automated synapse detection in conventionally stained and fixated 3D EM data, in which neurite contact is most frequent at non-synaptic sites.

query: Such data are widely used, and acquiring such data does not require special fixation protocols.
matched_segment: Such data are widely used, and acquiring such data does not require special fixation protocols.

query: So far, the classification of synapses into inhibitory (symmetric) vs. excitatory (asymmetric) was carried out for a given single synapse, often in single cross sections of single synapses (e.g. Colonnier, 1968). With the increasing availability of large-scale 3D EM datasets, however, synapse types can be defined based on multiple synapses of the same axon (e.g. Kasthuri et al., 2015).
matched_segment: So far, the classification of synapses into inhibitory (symmetric) vs. excitatory (asymmetric) was carried out for a given single synapse, often in single cross sections of single synapses (e.g. Colonnier, 1968). With the increasing availability of large-scale 3D EM datasets, however, synapse types can be defined based on multiple synapses of the same axon (e.g. Kasthuri et al., 2015).

query: In the case of a dataset sized a cubic millimeter of cortical tissue, most axons of interneurons will be fully contained in the dataset since most inhibitory neurons are local.
matched_segment: In the case of a dataset sized a cubic millimeter of cortical tissue, most axons of interneurons will be fully contained in the dataset since most inhibitory neurons are local.

query: Consequently, the classification of single synapses can be replaced by the assignment of synapses to the respective axon; the type of axon is then inferred from the neurons' somatic and dendritic features.
matched_segment: Consequently, the classification of single synapses can be replaced by the assignment of synapses to the respective axon; the type of axon is then inferred from the neurons' somatic and dendritic features.

query: Even for axons which are not completely contained in the dataset, the assignment to inhibitory or excitatory synaptic phenotypes can be based on dozens or hundreds rather than single synapses.
matched_segment: Even for axons which are not completely contained in the dataset, the assignment to inhibitory or excitatory synaptic phenotypes can be based on dozens or hundreds rather than single synapses.

query: Together, SynEM resolves synapse detection for high-throughput cortical connectomics of mammalian brains, removing synapse detection as a bottleneck in connectomics.
matched_segment: Together, SynEM resolves synapse detection for high-throughput cortical connectomics of mammalian brains, removing synapse detection as a bottleneck in connectomics.

query: With this, SynEM renders the further acceleration of neurite reconstruction again the key challenge for future connectomic analysis.
matched_segment: With this, SynEM renders the further acceleration of neurite reconstruction again the key challenge for future connectomic analysis.
